markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least one genuine fraction from their own Number Line Track or Face-Off Ring trials that was greater than 1/2, and one that was less than 1/2 (actual numerator/denominator values from their own Investigation Record).
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine trials from the student's own record, correctly sorted into 'greater than 1/2' and 'less than 1/2'.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim with no actual fraction values quoted from their own trials.

markingScheme.criterion: States the general rule correctly: a fraction is greater than 1/2 exactly when its numerator is more than half its denominator (equivalently, 2 x numerator > denominator), and less than 1/2 when 2 x numerator < denominator.
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent correct phrasing, e.g. comparing the numerator to half the denominator, or cross-multiplying against 1/2.

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly applies this rule to check their own quoted example(s) from point 1, showing the rule actually explains the result they observed.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating the numeric rule correctly with no link back to their own quoted trial(s).

markingScheme.criterion: (a) Correctly multiplies 2/3 x 3/4, giving 6/12 = 1/2 cup (or an equivalent correct fraction/decimal).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct working that arrives at an equivalent value to 1/2 (e.g. 0.5 cup).
markingScheme.insufficient: Adding or otherwise combining the fractions instead of multiplying, or an arithmetic slip in the multiplication.

markingScheme.criterion: (b) Correctly estimates using benchmarks — recognises 2/3 is close to 1/2 (or close to its own value) and 1/4 is close to 1/4 or 0, and concludes the total is a little less than 1 cup (the exact total, 11/12, is indeed just under 1) — stating clearly whether the estimate is more or less than 1.
markingScheme.accept: Any reasonable benchmark-based reasoning (e.g. rounding 2/3 up towards 1 and 1/4 down towards 0) that reaches a correct more/less-than-1 conclusion.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating an answer with no benchmark reasoning shown, or reaching the wrong side of 1.

markingScheme.criterion: (c) Explains why multiplying by a fraction smaller than 1 gives a smaller result, referencing their own multiplication grid evidence (e.g. the shaded overlap region is smaller than either whole strip/column, because you are taking 'a fraction of a fraction').
markingScheme.insufficient: A general statement that 'multiplying fractions makes them smaller' with no reference to the grid model or to why this happens.

levels.descriptor: Achieves 0 of the 3 points above: no genuine trial figures are quoted, no general 1/2-comparison rule is stated, and the rule is not linked back to their own example.

Achieves 1 of the 3 points above — most commonly quotes at least one real trial (a fraction they actually placed or compared) but does not state the general rule correctly and/or does not apply it back to their own example.
Achieves 2 of the 3 points above — e.g. quotes genuine trial fractions and states the general rule correctly, but does not clearly apply the rule back to verify their own quoted example(s).
Achieves all 3 of the points above: quotes genuine 'greater than 1/2' and 'less than 1/2' trials from their own record, states the general rule correctly, and applies it to check their own examples.

levels.descriptor: Achieves 0 of the 3 points above: the multiplication in (a) is not correct, the benchmark estimate in (b) is missing or wrong, and (c) gives no grid-based explanation.
Achieves 1 of the 3 points above — most commonly correctly multiplies 2/3 x 3/4 in (a), but does not correctly estimate using benchmarks in (b) and/or does not explain (c) using grid evidence.
Achieves 2 of the 3 points above — e.g. correctly multiplies in (a) and estimates correctly using benchmarks in (b), but does not also explain (c) with reference to the multiplication grid.

Achieves all 3 of the points above: correctly multiplies 2/3 x 3/4 in (a), correctly estimates whether the sum in (b) is more or less than 1 using benchmark reasoning, and explains in (c) why multiplying by a fraction less than 1 shrinks the result, using their own grid evidence.

markingInstructions: This is a Primary 2 student. Mark ONLY the two constructed responses, using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme in marking_context (award each point independently unless it names a dependsOn point, in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded) and each point's accept/insufficient wording. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points (one per lettered part a/b/c) — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Accept valid alternative wording or equivalent fractions/decimals; do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 14 (6 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
